corpus.shape: mixed rotation: add, modify, delete, rename, binary, mode-only, multi-file, trailer blocks, a non-UTF-8 path, one over-cap blob, and two merge commits

budget.source: `benchmarks/budgets.json`; the ticket's own 500-commit fixture is the `small` class

notes: parallel speedup on the normalize phase was 2.15x against one worker, with 500 commits on 8 cpus; the store write is one transaction per batch and is deliberately serial, so this ratio is the diffable half - and at a few hundred commits the diffs are too small for the pool to show much
batches were 512 commits (about 1024 rows, counting a commit row plus its file rows), inside ADR-004 7.3's write.batch_rows of 5 000
cold = first ingest in this process; the OS page cache is not dropped (that needs root), so a first run on a cold machine will be slower than this
`cold_index_ms` is walk + normalize + one SQLite transaction per batch, into a WAL database with synchronous=NORMAL, which is ADR-004 §7's configuration and not a benchmark expedient
`already_indexed_ms` is the resume floor: the walk still runs, so it is a lower bound on re-running against a store that is already current, not a measurement of skipped work
`git_log_numstat_ms` is context, not a competitor: git does not normalize, dedupe, or write anything, and fathom never shells out to it (ADR-001 §8.2)
no `ingest.*` latency family exists in benchmarks/budgets.json; `cold.index.ms` is the family this ticket actually has a budget in, and the caps are `ingest.file_size_cap.mib`
